question: What specifically does the Masked-Prediction Feature Extraction Module in the 2025 single-stage framework predict, and how does it explicitly handle audio-visual alignment bypass attacks?
ground_truth: The module predicts the next frame's features from previous frames using two unimodal modules and one cross-modal module. By checking within-modality and cross-modality discrepancies explicitly, it can detect local inconsistencies even when an attack preserves cross-modal audio-visual alignment.
expected_source: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization.pdf

question: In the Undercover Deepfakes architecture, what precise role does Scaling and Shifting (SSF) play when fine-tuning the spatial feature extractor?
ground_truth: Scaling and Shifting (SSF) modulates deep features to alleviate the distribution mismatch between the pre-trained task (ImageNet-21K) and the downstream deepfake feature extraction task by introducing scale and shift parameters after each operation while keeping original network parameters frozen.
expected_source: Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos.pdf

question: Compare the core temporal modeling mechanisms used by Anshul et al. (2025) versus Saha et al. (2023) to establish boundaries for localized fake segments.
ground_truth: Anshul et al. utilize a Causal Transformer Encoder/Decoder to model temporal context alongside a localized Convolutional Cross-Attention window (w=9) and a multi-level feature pyramid (PCA-FPN). In contrast, Saha et al. employ a Timeseries Transformer (TsT) processing sequentially windowed feature vectors combined with a post-processing sliding window smoothing algorithm (size 15) using majority voting.
expected_source: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization.pdf; Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos.pdf

question: How do the modal inputs differ fundamentally between the RAG indexed papers when executing temporal localization tasks?
ground_truth: The framework by Anshul et al. is fundamentally multimodal, extracting and fusing both audio (ViT encoder) and visual (AV-HuBERT ResNet-18) features to capture inter- and intra-modal errors. Conversely, the framework by Saha et al. focuses strictly on the visual modality, performing face extraction/alignment and tracking spatial-temporal variances across video frames.
expected_source: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization.pdf; Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos.pdf

question: What optimization loss functions are introduced by the 2025 Next-Frame prediction model to explicitly guide the separation of real and deepfake frame representations?
ground_truth: The model incorporates an average frame-level contrastive loss calculated across three separate streams (audio, visual, and audio-visual). It works alongside binary cross-entropy or regression losses to pull predicted and actual frame features closer for real samples while pushing them apart for deepfakes.
expected_source: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization.pdf

question: According to the dataset construction descriptions in both text indices, what are the average lengths or ratios typically associated with localized fake injection windows?
ground_truth: In the LAV-DF dataset used by Anshul et al., fake segments range from 0 to 1.6 seconds with an average length of 0.65 seconds (89.26% under 1 second). In the dataset built by Saha et al. using FF++, fake frames average 24.3% of the video for single-segment fakes and 41.1% for two-segment fakes, with segment lengths manually targeted or randomly sampled at lengths like 125, 150, or 175 frames.
expected_source: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization.pdf; Undercover Deepfakes: Detecting Fake Segments in Videos.pdf
